The MatX One chip is designed with a splittable systolic array architecture that the company says delivers higher throughput than any announced system while also achieving low latency through a hybrid SRAM-first design combined with high-bandwidth memory for long-context support.

The company said it was founded on the belief that the best LLM processor should be designed from first principles with a deep understanding of evolving model needs. MatX, an AI chip startup founded by former Google hardware engineers Reiner Pope and Mike Gunter, announced a $500 million Series B funding round on February 24, 2026, positioning itself as a direct challenger to Nvidia's dominance in AI processor markets[1]. The round was led by investment firms Jane Street and Situational Awareness, signaling substantial investor confidence in alternative AI hardware solutions.

MatX plans to manufacture its chips through TSMC, the world's leading semiconductor foundry, with initial shipments scheduled for 2027[1]. This manufacturing partnership and timeline align with industry projections for next-generation AI hardware requirements as computational demands for large language models continue to escalate[1]. The $500 million funding injection provides the necessary capital to support the capital-intensive chip development and production process. MatX's funding announcement represents one of the largest Series B rounds in semiconductor history[1]. The broader AI chip sector demonstrated significant momentum, with AI chip startups collectively raising more than $1.1 billion in funding as of Tuesday, February 25, 2026, despite ongoing concerns about an AI bubble[2]. MatX received the lion's share of this capital among competing AI hardware startups[2].

The $500 million Series B represents a major escalation from MatX's previous Series A round of approximately $100 million led by Spark Capital[1]. Beyond the lead investors, the funding consortium includes Marvell Technology, NFDG, Spark Capital, and Stripe co-founders Patrick Collison and John Collison[1]. Situational Awareness, founded by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, brings particular credibility given its founder's deep expertise in AI computational requirements from the model development perspective[1].
